title: One-Minute Launch: Developer Script + Pricing Language
content:
Purpose
This is a compact, testable go-to-market brief that we can use for landing page microcopy, signup flows, and the 1-minute demo script for the Hosted API. Focus: developer-first language, crystal-clear cost framing, and a few alternate pricing phrasings to A/B test.

Audience
- Primary: Software engineers and ML engineers who need to ship an LLM integration in hours, not weeks.
- Secondary: Platform and engineering managers evaluating cost & predictable performance.

Core one-liner options (pick one per page/test)
1) "Ship an LLM endpoint in 60s — reliable latency, predictable cost."
2) "From zero to a token stream: one call, local tooling, measurable unit cost."
3) "Hosted inference that behaves like your dev tooling — fast, debuggable, and affordable."

Why this resonates (dev-centric rationale)
- Time-to-first-success matters: devs want a working request/response with minimal config.
- Observability and cost clarity reduce friction to basic adoption (if I can see token cost per request, I’ll try more).
- Familiarity: describe the API like a simple HTTP client call — reduces cognitive load vs platform-speak.

Quickstart demo script (60–90s spoken + 2 code snippets)
- Hook (10s): "Want a working assistant in one minute? Paste this snippet into your existing backend and call /v1/complete."
- Show code (20s): one cURL + one Node/Go snippet that returns a streaming response. Keep headers small (api-key, model, stream:true).
- Show cost line (10s): show the response with a small overlay: "~0.6¢ per 256 token response — tracked in Console > Usage."
- Close (20s): "Signup takes <60s. Free credits for first 30 days. No infra changes, just an API key."

Suggested quickstart microcopy (for signup & first-run)
- Signup success: "API key created — welcome! Your first $50 in credits expires in 30 days."
- First call success modal: "Nice! Your first API call succeeded. Estimated cost: 0.006 USD. View detailed cost & latency in Console."
- Error guidance: "Request failed — check model, key, and region. See Troubleshooting > connection issues."

Pricing-language drafts (three clear approaches to A/B test)
A — Simple per-token anchor (baseline)
- "Inference pricing: pay only for tokens generated and processed. Example: a 256-token assistant reply costs ~0.6¢."
- Pros: transparent, matches dev mental model.
- Cons: needs helpers to estimate per-session costs.

B — Unitized sessions for simplified buyer decisions
- "Session units: small (50 units/month), team (2,000 units/month). One session unit covers a typical single-turn assistant reply (~256 tokens)."
- Pros: easier for managers to budget.
- Cons: obfuscates real per-token economics for power users.

C — Hybrid: per-token with packaged commitments for teams
- "Pay per token; reserve team packs for predictable throughput and 10–20% unit discount. Reserved packs include priority routing and longer KV-cache retention."
- Pros: clean upgrade path to Dedicated; maps to our product tiers.

Pricing microcopy examples (UI-ready)
- Landing price snippet: "Getting started: ~0.6¢ per 256-token reply. Free $50 credits for new accounts."
- Upsell for reserved capacity: "Need predictable throughput? Reserve capacity and save up to 20% per token. Contact Sales for enterprise pricing."

Competitive positioning bullets (developer lens)
- Against hyperscalers: emphasize dev ergonomics + predictable latency vs opaque autoscaling costs. "Less ops, more observability."
- Against LLM-only APIs (simplicity-first): emphasize performance controls (batching, cache), model catalog, and rollouts — not just model access. "Control cost without losing simplicity."
- Against self-hosted stacks: emphasize no infra management + optimized kernels and SLA-backed routing. "Same performance assumptions, without the infra."

Objection handling (short replies for support / chatbots)
- "How do you keep latency low?" -> "Smart routing, optimized kernels, and aggressive prefix caching — typical p95 for short conversations is <120ms in hosted regions."
- "What if token cost spikes?" -> "Set per-route guards, fallbacks, and alerted thresholds in Console. You control routing and quantization profiles."
- "Can I run in my VPC?" -> "Yes — Redwood Private has a near-identical API and the same Console UX."

Call-to-action experiments (A/B candidates)
1) "Get your free $50 credits — create an endpoint in 60s" (focus on credits + speed)
2) "Run a demo in your console — 1-minute setup" (focus on product-first)
3) "Compare latency & cost vs your current provider" (focus on evaluation)

Success metrics to track for each CTA
- Time-to-first-success (TTFS): median time from signup -> first successful API call (goal: <5m).
- Activation rate: percent of accounts that make >=3 calls within 24h.
- Cost clarity lift: survey NPS question after first run — did you understand cost impact? (target 80% yes)

Copy experiments and test matrix (quick plan)
- Variant 1: per-token anchor on hero + code-first demo. Track TTFS and activation.
- Variant 2: package units framing with explicit team pack CTA. Track MQLs and upgrade trials.
- Variant 3: hybrid hero (cost + reserved capacity) aimed at small platform teams. Track demo requests and contact-sales conversions.

Notes to product / docs teams (action items)
- Create a one-click code snippet generator in Console that returns estimated token cost per example. (JIRA-RT-314)
- Add a first-call modal that surfaces estimated per-call cost and link to cost-explainer doc.
- Provide downloadable quickstart gist for Node/Python/Go with streaming and error-handling examples.

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs
- How explicit should we be about per-token math on hero vs deeper docs? (tradeoff: conversion vs accuracy)
- Do we expose session units as a formal product or keep it as a pricing UI abstraction?
- Is $50 the right starter credit? Benchmark vs competitors & elasticity.

Appendix: short testing timeline (8 weeks)
- Week 1: landing page variants + one-click snippets ready in Console.
- Weeks 2–3: run A/B tests, monitor TTFS & activation.
- Weeks 4–6: iterate on highest-performing microcopy and deploy to onboarding email flows.
- Week 8: review MQL conversions and recommend pricing language to Sales enablement.

Slack note (copyable):
"@growth FYI — pushing a 1-minute launch brief into the landing page tests. Goal: raise TTFS and make per-call cost visible on first run. See Confluence INF-482 for longer rationale."

——
Author notes: keep language simple, avoid platform jargon, and always show a tangible cost example (numbers beat adjectives). This doc is intentionally compact so we can move quickly.
